guidance: Check what each external connection exchanges, why it is needed and what happens on failure. Add actual interface references, without entering real secrets.
bundleDescription:
- **Capability**: design each product-relevant external connection as a complete new Plugin, with concise product-side notes.
- **Resolves**: S/T gaps around which external capability the product needs, how the Agent accesses and uses it, and what the product does when the connection succeeds or fails.
- **Candidate when**: a product behavior depends on an external API, webhook, SDK, MCP tool, third-party component, device, or team-operated system.
- **Do not infer**: never invent vendor behavior, URL, credential, endpoint, or field-level API contract.
- **Output**: `integration_design` panel — one editable Plugin-style connection record plus product-side remarks for every external capability.
empty: No integrations yet. Add connection instructions and product-side rules as needed.
title: Name
descriptionHelp: In one sentence, explain what this connection does for the product.
descriptionExample: For example: create a warehouse shipment and return its identifier.
urlHelp: Enter the confirmed service endpoint or documentation address.
secretsHelp: Record credential names and purposes only. Configure actual secrets through the host credential service, never in Design Files. Leave this empty if authentication is unnecessary.
secretName: Credential name (uppercase letters, digits and underscores)
promptHelp: Explain when to use the connection, what to do, and which results to return.
promptExample: For example: after order approval, submit confirmed order details and return shipment identification and status.
notesHelp: Describe product triggers, success and failure handling without repeating API fields.
notesExample: For example: keep the shipment identifier on success; preserve the order on failure and offer retry without duplication.
